La Comida y la Bebida — Food and Drink

Food and drink is one of the most commonly tested topics in AQA GCSE Spanish. It appears in Theme 1: People and Lifestyle and can come up across all four exam papers. You need to know food vocabulary, talk about mealtimes, express preferences, and order food. This lesson also covers the useful phrase me gustaría (I would like) for expressing polite desires and wishes.

Fruit & Vegetables (frutas y verduras):
la manzana — apple | la naranja — orange | el plátano — banana
la fresa — strawberry | la pera — pear | la piña — pineapple
el melocotón — peach | las uvas — grapes
la verdura — vegetable | la ensalada — salad
la patata — potato | el tomate — tomato
la zanahoria — carrot | los guisantes — peas

Meat & Fish (carne y pescado):
la carne — meat | el pollo — chicken
el cerdo — pork | el cordero — lamb
el bistec — steak | el jamón — ham
el pescado — fish | los mariscos — seafood
las gambas — prawns | los calamares — squid

Other food:
el pan — bread | el arroz — rice | la pasta — pasta
el queso — cheese | el huevo — egg
los cereales — cereal | las patatas fritas — chips
la paella — paella | las tapas — tapas
el helado — ice cream | el pastel — cake
el bocadillo — sandwich | el churro — churro
las galletas — biscuits | los dulces — sweets

el agua — water (note: feminine despite el)
la leche — milk | el zumo — juice
el café — coffee | el té — tea
el refresco — soft drink | la limonada — lemonade
las bebidas azucaradas — sugary drinks

Las Comidas del Día — Meals of the Day

Spanish-speaking countries have slightly different meal times and traditions compared to the UK. Understanding these differences can help you in the reading and listening exams.

Key Fact

The three main meals in Spanish are:
El desayuno — breakfast (usually light: coffee, toast, cereal)
La comida / el almuerzo — lunch (the main meal in Spain, typically 2–3pm)
La cena — dinner/supper (lighter, typically 9–10pm in Spain)
La merienda — afternoon snack (around 5–6pm)
The verbs for these are: desayunar (to have breakfast), almorzar/comer (to have lunch), cenar (to have dinner), merendar (to have an afternoon snack).

Here are useful phrases for discussing meals:

Para el desayuno, normalmente como tostadas con mantequilla. — For breakfast, I normally eat toast with butter.
Almuerzo en el instituto a las doce y media. — I have lunch at school at half past twelve.
Cenamos en familia a las ocho de la noche. — We have dinner as a family at eight in the evening.
Ayer desayuné cereales con leche. — Yesterday I had cereal with milk for breakfast.

Expressing Food Preferences

Being able to express what you like and dislike eating is essential. You need to go beyond me gusta and use a range of food opinion adjectives to impress the examiner.

Positive opinions:
Me encanta — I love | Me chifla / Me flipa — I’m crazy about (informal)
delicioso/a — delicious | sabroso/a — tasty
rico/a — rich, delicious | riquísimo/a — really delicious
¡Hizo la boca agua! — It was mouth-watering!

Negative opinions:
No me gusta (nada) — I don’t like (at all) | No aguanto — I can’t stand
Odio — I hate | Detesto — I detest
asqueroso/a — disgusting | repugnante — revolting
malo/a — bad | horrible — horrible

Examples:
Me encanta la paella porque es muy sabrosa. — I love paella because it is very tasty.
No aguanto el pescado — es asqueroso. — I can’t stand fish — it’s disgusting.
La comida española es riquísima. — Spanish food is really delicious.

Me Gustaría — I Would Like

The phrase me gustaría (I would like) is the conditional form of gustar and is extremely useful across many topics. It is a polite way to express what you would like to eat, drink or do.

Key Fact

Me gustaría + infinitive = I would like to …
Me gustaría probar la paella. — I would like to try paella.
Me gustaría comer en un restaurante español. — I would like to eat in a Spanish restaurant.
Me gustaría beber un zumo de naranja. — I would like to drink an orange juice.
Also useful: Quisiera — I would like (very formal/polite, from querer).

Using the Past Tense with Food

To talk about what you ate and drank, use the preterite tense. Key verbs include:

Comer (to eat): comí (I ate), comiste (you ate), comió (he/she ate), comimos (we ate), comieron (they ate)
Beber (to drink): bebí (I drank), bebiste (you drank), bebió (he/she drank)
Desayunar: desayuné (I had breakfast)
Cenar: cené (I had dinner)

Example sentences in the preterite:
Ayer comí paella y bebí limonada. — Yesterday I ate paella and drank lemonade.
Anoche cenamos en un restaurante italiano. — Last night we had dinner at an Italian restaurant.
El fin de semana pasado, desayuné churros con chocolate. — Last weekend, I had churros with chocolate for breakfast.

Me encanta la comida española, especialmente la paella y las tapas. Para el desayuno, normalmente como tostadas con mermelada y bebo un zumo de naranja. A mediodía, almuerzo en el instituto — generalmente como un bocadillo de jamón y queso. Cenamos en familia a las siete. Mi plato favorito es la tortilla española porque es muy sabrosa. Ayer cené pescado con patatas fritas y estaba riquísimo. Me gustaría probar más comida española en el futuro — especialmente los churros con chocolate.

Translation: I love Spanish food, especially paella and tapas. For breakfast, I normally eat toast with jam and drink an orange juice. At midday, I have lunch at school — I usually eat a ham and cheese sandwich. We have dinner as a family at seven. My favourite dish is Spanish omelette because it is very tasty. Yesterday I had fish with chips for dinner and it was really delicious. I would like to try more Spanish food in the future — especially churros with chocolate.

This model uses three tenses — present (como, bebo, cenamos), preterite (cené, estaba), and conditional (me gustaría) — which is essential for accessing the higher mark bands in writing and speaking.

Music, Film and Television

Being able to talk about your favourite music, films and TV programmes is a key part of AQA GCSE Spanish Theme 2. The exam tests whether you can describe what you watch and listen to, give opiniones (opinions) about it, and justify those opinions with reasons. This topic appears in all four papers — listening, speaking, reading and writing.

In this lesson, you will learn the vocabulary for different types of music, film and TV genres, how to express what you like and dislike, and how to write extended answers that impress the examiner.

Music Vocabulary

Music genres: la música pop (pop music), la música clásica (classical music), el rap (rap), el rock (rock), la música electrónica (electronic music), el reguetón (reggaeton), el flamenco (flamenco), la música latina (Latin music).

Useful phrases: “Mi cantante favorito/a es…” (My favourite singer is…), “Suelo escuchar…” (I usually listen to…), “Me pone de buen humor” (It puts me in a good mood), “Escucho música todos los días” (I listen to music every day).

Key Fact

Me encanta means “I love (it)” and me aburre means “it bores me.” These are verbos de tipo gustar (verbs like gustar) — the thing you like is the subject. So “me encantan las películas de acción” uses the plural encantan because “las películas” is plural.

Film and Television Vocabulary

Film genres: una película de acción (action film), una película de terror (horror film), una película romántica (romantic film), una comedia (comedy), una película de ciencia ficción (sci-fi film), una película de aventuras (adventure film), un documental (documentary), una película de dibujos animados (cartoon/animated film).

TV programmes: un programa de televisión (TV programme), un concurso (game show), las noticias (the news), una serie (series), un reality (reality show), un programa de deportes (sports programme), los dibujos animados (cartoons), una telenovela (soap opera).

Expressing Likes and Dislikes

To access higher marks, you need a range of ways to say what you like and dislike. Here is a scale from most positive to most negative:

  • Me encanta / Me fascina / Me chifla — I love it / It fascinates me / I’m crazy about it
  • Me gusta mucho / Me mola — I really like it / It’s cool
  • Me gusta bastante — I quite like it
  • No me gusta / No me interesa — I don’t like it / It doesn’t interest me
  • Me aburre / Me molesta / No soporto — It bores me / It annoys me / I can’t stand it
  • Odio / Detesto — I hate / I detest

Adjectives for Describing Entertainment

Use a variety of adjetivos (adjectives) to describe why you like or dislike something:

  • Positive: divertido/a (fun), emocionante (exciting), interesante (interesting), genial (great), guay (cool), increíble (incredible), entretenido/a (entertaining), conmovedor/a (moving).
  • Negative: aburrido/a (boring), tonto/a (silly), lento/a (slow), repetitivo/a (repetitive), horroroso/a (horrible), una pérdida de tiempo (a waste of time).
Key Fact

Remember that adjectives in Spanish must agree with the noun they describe. A masculine singular noun takes the -o ending (divertido), a feminine singular noun takes -a (divertida), and plurals add -s or -es. Getting agreements right shows good grammar and earns marks for accuracy.

Mi película favorita es una comedia que se llama “Ocho apellidos vascos.” Me encanta porque es muy divertida y los personajes son graciosos. Normalmente prefiero las películas de acción ya que son emocionantes, pero esta comedia me hizo reír mucho. No me gustan las películas de terror porque me dan miedo. En mi opinión, ver películas es la mejor manera de relajarse después de un día largo en el instituto.

Translation: My favourite film is a comedy called “Spanish Affair.” I love it because it is very funny and the characters are hilarious. I normally prefer action films since they are exciting, but this comedy made me laugh a lot. I don’t like horror films because they scare me. In my opinion, watching films is the best way to relax after a long day at school.

The Environment — Global Issues

The environment is a key topic in AQA GCSE Spanish Theme 3, especially at Higher Tier. You need to discuss environmental problems, say what you and others do to help, and describe what should be done in the future. This topic also links to your local area and global awareness.

Key Fact

the specification expects you to discuss environmental issues using multiple tenses: what you do now (present), what you did (preterite), and what you will do or should do (future / conditional). The phrases se debe (one must) and deberíamos (we should) are essential for this topic.

Key Vocabulary — Environmental Problems

el medio ambiente — the environment. la contaminación — pollution. el cambio climático — climate change. el calentamiento global — global warming. la basura — rubbish. el reciclaje — recycling. los residuos — waste. la deforestación — deforestation. las especies en peligro — endangered species. el efecto invernadero — the greenhouse effect. las energías renovables — renewable energy. la contaminación del aire — air pollution. la contaminación del agua — water pollution. los gases de escape — exhaust fumes.

Describing Environmental Problems

Key phrases for discussing problems:

Hay mucha contaminación en las ciudades — There is a lot of pollution in cities. El cambio climático es un problema grave — Climate change is a serious problem. Hay demasiada basura en las calles — There is too much rubbish in the streets. Los coches causan la contaminación del aire — Cars cause air pollution. La deforestación destruye los hábitats naturales — Deforestation destroys natural habitats.

Key Fact

For the Higher Tier, use complex opinion phrases: Creo que el cambio climático es el problema más importante de nuestro tiempo — I think climate change is the most important problem of our time. Me preocupa mucho la contaminación — Pollution worries me a lot.

What We Do to Help

reciclar — to recycle. reutilizar — to reuse. reducir — to reduce. ahorrar agua — to save water. ahorrar energía — to save energy. apagar las luces — to turn off the lights. ir en bici — to go by bike. usar el transporte público — to use public transport. no malgastar agua — not to waste water. comprar productos locales — to buy local products. plantar árboles — to plant trees. proteger el medio ambiente — to protect the environment.

The source material provides this model from the mosaic translations: “Hago todo lo posible para proteger el medio ambiente. Reciclo, no malgasto agua y voy en bici al instituto.” — I do everything possible to protect the environment. I recycle, I don’t waste water, and I go to school by bike.

What We Should Do — Obligations and the Future

Use these structures to say what we should or must do:

Se debe + infinitive — One must… (Se debe reciclar más — One must recycle more.) Deberíamos + infinitive — We should… (Deberíamos usar menos plástico — We should use less plastic.) Hay que + infinitive — It is necessary to… (Hay que proteger el medio ambiente — It is necessary to protect the environment.) Es importante + infinitive — It is important to… (Es importante ahorrar energía — It is important to save energy.)

Key Fact

The future tense is formed by adding endings to the infinitive: -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án. Example: Reciclaré más en el futuro — I will recycle more in the future. Usaremos energías renovables — We will use renewable energy.

Some verbs have irregular stems in the future tense (same as the conditional): tener → tendré (I will have), hacer → haré (I will do), poder → podré (I will be able to), salir → saldré (I will go out), haber → habrá (there will be), poner → pondré (I will put), querer → querré (I will want).

School and Community Action

The source material’s mosaic translation provides a school-based example: “Para ser un instituto verde, hacemos muchas cosas para ayudar el medio ambiente. Por ejemplo, el mes pasado hicimos un jardín donde plantamos árboles. Además, vamos a empezar un programa de reciclaje.”

This model shows three tenses in one paragraph: present (hacemos), preterite (hicimos, plantamos), and near future (vamos a empezar). This is exactly what the examiner wants to see.

Key Fact

Use fancy phrases from the source material to elevate your writing: A pesar de eso… (Despite that…), Estoy convencido/a de que… (I am convinced that…), Deberíamos… (We should…), Vale la pena mencionar que… (It’s worth mentioning that…).

La Vida Sana — Healthy Living

Healthy living is a core topic in AQA GCSE Spanish Theme 1: People and Lifestyle. You need to discuss what you do to stay healthy, talk about diet and exercise, and give advice on healthy habits. This topic tests your ability to use modal verbs and express obligation — key grammar for the higher mark bands.

la salud — health
sano/a — healthy
en forma — fit, in shape
la dieta — diet
equilibrado/a — balanced
la comida — food, meal
la bebida — drink
el ejercicio — exercise
el deporte — sport
el cuerpo — body
el estrés — stress
la obesidad — obesity
gordo/a — fat | delgado/a — slim
fuerte — strong | débil — weak

Verbs:
mantenerse en forma — to keep fit
hacer ejercicio — to do exercise
dormir — to sleep
relajarse — to relax
fumar — to smoke
beber alcohol — to drink alcohol
evitar — to avoid
mejorar — to improve

Expressing Obligation — Se Debe / No Se Debe

One of the most useful structures for this topic is expressing what you should or shouldn’t do. Spanish has several ways to express obligation, and the exam rewards students who use a variety of these structures.

Key Fact

There are three key ways to express obligation in Spanish:
1. Se debe + infinitive — One should / You should (impersonal)
2. Deber + infinitive — To must / should (personal, conjugated)
3. Tener que + infinitive — To have to (personal, conjugated)
For example: Se debe comer bien (One should eat well), Debes hacer ejercicio (You must do exercise), Tengo que dormir más (I have to sleep more).

Deber (must, should) + infinitive:
Debo comer más fruta — I must eat more fruit
Debes evitar la comida rápida — You should avoid fast food
Debemos hacer ejercicio cada día — We should exercise every day

Tener que (have to) + que + infinitive:
Tengo que beber más agua — I have to drink more water
Tienes que dormir ocho horas — You have to sleep eight hours
Tenemos que evitar el estrés — We have to avoid stress

Poder (can, to be able to) + infinitive:
Puedo ir al gimnasio — I can go to the gym
No puedes fumar — You cannot smoke
Podemos mejorar nuestra dieta — We can improve our diet

Remember: After a modal verb, always use the infinitive form of the second verb. A common mistake is conjugating both verbs: *Debo como is wrong — it should be Debo comer.

Healthy and Unhealthy Habits

The exam often asks you to discuss what is healthy and unhealthy. Use the following structure: Para mantenerse en forma, se debe… (To keep fit, one should…) and No se debe… (One shouldn’t…).

Healthy habits (hábitos saludables):
Se debe comer una dieta equilibrada. — One should eat a balanced diet.
Se debe beber mucha agua. — One should drink lots of water.
Se debe hacer ejercicio con regularidad. — One should exercise regularly.
Se debe dormir ocho horas cada noche. — One should sleep eight hours every night.
Se debe comer frutas y verduras. — One should eat fruits and vegetables.

Unhealthy habits (hábitos no saludables):
No se debe fumar. — One shouldn’t smoke.
No se debe beber alcohol. — One shouldn’t drink alcohol.
No se debe comer demasiada comida rápida. — One shouldn’t eat too much fast food.
No se debe tomar drogas. — One shouldn’t take drugs.
No se debe beber bebidas azucaradas. — One shouldn’t drink sugary drinks.

Key Fact

The word equilibrada (balanced) is essential for this topic. The phrase una dieta equilibrada (a balanced diet) appears frequently in AQA reading and listening exams. Notice the adjective ending: equilibrada has the feminine -a ending because dieta is feminine.

Talking About Your Own Lifestyle

In the speaking and writing exams, you need to describe your own lifestyle habits. Use a mixture of what you do (como, bebo, hago) and what you should do (debo, tengo que) to show range.

Useful phrases:
Normalmente como frutas y verduras. — I normally eat fruits and vegetables.
Bebo mucha agua todos los días. — I drink lots of water every day.
Hago deporte tres veces a la semana. — I do sport three times a week.
Intento evitar la comida rápida. — I try to avoid fast food.
Debería hacer más ejercicio. — I should do more exercise. (conditional of deber)
No duermo lo suficiente. — I don’t sleep enough.

Para mantenerse en forma, se debe llevar una vida sana. Personalmente, intento comer una dieta equilibrada con mucha fruta y verdura. Bebo al menos dos litros de agua cada día y hago deporte tres veces a la semana — juego al fútbol y hago natación. Sin embargo, debo admitir que a veces como demasiada comida rápida y no duermo lo suficiente. Debería dormir ocho horas pero normalmente solo duermo seis. En el futuro, me gustaría mejorar mi dieta y hacer más ejercicio.

Translation: To keep fit, one should lead a healthy life. Personally, I try to eat a balanced diet with lots of fruit and vegetables. I drink at least two litres of water every day and I do sport three times a week — I play football and I do swimming. However, I must admit that sometimes I eat too much fast food and I don’t sleep enough. I should sleep eight hours but I normally only sleep six. In the future, I would like to improve my diet and do more exercise.

This model uses the present tense (como, bebo, hago), modal verbs (debo admitir, debería dormir), the impersonal se debe, and the conditional (me gustaría). This mix of structures and frequency expressions (a veces, normalmente, cada día, tres veces a la semana) is exactly what examiners look for.

Types of Accommodation

When discussing holidays in the AQA GCSE Spanish exam, you need to describe where you stayed, book accommodation, and deal with problems. This topic tests your ability to use vocabulary for different types of lodgings and to communicate in practical situations.

Key Fact

The exam may ask you to role-play booking a hotel room or to write about your alojamiento (accommodation). Learn both the vocabulary and the functional phrases for making bookings.

Key Vocabulary — Accommodation

un hotel — a hotel. un hotel de lujo — a luxury hotel. un albergue juvenil — a youth hostel. un camping — a campsite. una casa rural — a rural house / holiday cottage. una habitación individual — a single room. una habitación doble — a double room. con baño — with a bathroom. con vistas al mar — with sea views. media pensión — half board. pensión completa — full board. la recepción — the reception. la llave — the key. el ascensor — the lift. la planta baja — the ground floor.

Booking a Hotel Room

In a role-play or writing task, you may need to book a room. Here are key phrases:

Quisiera reservar una habitación — I would like to book a room. ¿Tiene habitaciones libres? — Do you have rooms available? Para dos noches — For two nights. ¿Cuánto cuesta por noche? — How much does it cost per night? Quiero una habitación doble con baño — I want a double room with a bathroom. ¿Está incluido el desayuno? — Is breakfast included?

Key Fact

Use quisiera (I would like) for polite requests in role-plays. It is more formal than quiero (I want) and shows the examiner you can vary your register.

Describing Where You Stayed

To describe past accommodation, use the preterite and imperfect tenses: Nos alojamos en una casa rural — We stayed in a holiday cottage. Me alojé en un hotel de lujo cerca de la playa — I stayed in a luxury hotel near the beach. El hotel era bonito y tenía piscina — The hotel was nice and had a pool. La habitación era grande y cómoda — The room was big and comfortable.

The imperfect tense is used here for descriptions of what the hotel was like, while the preterite is used for the action of staying there.

“El verano pasado me alojé en un hotel de lujo cerca de la playa. La habitación era grande y tenía vistas al mar. El hotel tenía una piscina enorme y un restaurante donde comíamos platos tradicionales. Me gustó mucho porque era muy cómodo y relajante.”

Dealing with Problems

You may be asked to complain or report a problem at a hotel. Key phrases include:

Hay un problema con la habitación — There is a problem with the room. No funciona el aire acondicionado — The air conditioning doesn’t work. No hay agua caliente — There is no hot water. La habitación está sucia — The room is dirty. El ascensor no funciona — The lift doesn’t work. Quisiera cambiar de habitación — I would like to change rooms. Quiero hacer una queja — I want to make a complaint.

To describe your ideal accommodation, use the conditional: Me alojaría en un hotel de lujo cerca de la playa — I would stay in a luxury hotel near the beach. Tendría vistas al mar y una piscina enorme — It would have sea views and a huge pool. Habría un restaurante donde comería platos tradicionales — There would be a restaurant where I would eat traditional dishes.

Key Fact

In role-play tasks about hotel problems, always use polite language such as quisiera and por favor. The examiner will give credit for appropriate register and for resolving the situation with clear communication.

Las Relaciones — Relationships

This lesson covers relationships and marriage — a topic that appears in AQA GCSE Spanish Theme 1: People and Lifestyle. You need to talk about different types of relationships, express views on marriage, and discuss future plans. This topic also introduces the conditional tense, which is essential for higher-level responses.

la relación — relationship
la pareja — couple, partner
el novio / la novia — boyfriend / girlfriend; groom / bride
el marido — husband | la mujer — wife, woman
la boda — wedding
el matrimonio — marriage
el amor — love
el cariño — affection
casado/a — married | soltero/a — single
casarse — to get married | divorciarse — to get divorced
separarse — to separate | enamorarse (de) — to fall in love (with)
romper (con) — to break up (with)

Example sentences:
Mis padres están casados desde hace veinte años. — My parents have been married for twenty years.
Mi hermana mayor se casó el año pasado. — My older sister got married last year.
No creo que el matrimonio sea necesario para ser feliz. — I don’t think marriage is necessary to be happy.

Views on Marriage

In the exam, you may be asked about your views on marriage and relationships. Some useful phrases include:

Quiero casarme algún día — I want to get married one day
No quiero casarme — I don’t want to get married
Me gustaría tener una familia grande — I would like to have a big family
Creo que el matrimonio es importante — I think marriage is important
En mi opinión, lo más importante es el amor — In my opinion, the most important thing is love
Hoy en día, muchas parejas prefieren no casarse — Nowadays, many couples prefer not to get married

Key Fact

In Spanish, casarse (to get married) is a reflexive verb. In the preterite: se casó (he/she got married), se casaron (they got married). In the future: me casaré (I will get married). Being able to use this verb in different tenses shows the examiner you have good grammatical range.

The Conditional Tense — El Condicional

The conditional tense is used to say what you would do. It is formed by adding specific endings to the infinitive of the verb. This tense is crucial for discussing hypothetical situations and future plans, and is rewarded in the higher mark bands of the writing and speaking exams.

Key Fact

The conditional tense endings are the same for -ar, -er, and -ir verbs. Add the endings directly to the infinitive: -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían. For example: hablar → hablaría (I would speak), comer → comería (I would eat), vivir → viviría (I would live).

Hablar (to speak):
Yo hablaría — I would speak
Tú hablarías — You would speak
Él/Ella hablaría — He/She would speak
Nosotros hablaríamos — We would speak
Vosotros hablaríais — You (pl.) would speak
Ellos/Ellas hablarían — They would speak

Example sentences:
Me casaría en una playa bonita. — I would get married on a beautiful beach.
Viviríamos en España si pudiéramos. — We would live in Spain if we could.
¿Te casarías algún día? — Would you get married one day?

Some common verbs have irregular stems in the conditional, but use the same endings (-ía, -ías, etc.):

tener → tendr- (tendría — I would have)
poder → podr- (podría — I would be able to / could)
querer → querr- (querría — I would want / like)
hacer → har- (haría — I would do/make)
ir → ir- (iría — I would go)
ser → ser- (sería — I would be)
salir → saldr- (saldría — I would go out)
poner → pondr- (pondría — I would put)

Note: Tener, poder, querer, hacer, salir and poner drop the -e- or -i- from the infinitive and sometimes add a -d- before the endings. Ser and ir keep their infinitive as the stem.

Talking About Future Plans

Combining the conditional with future time expressions helps you talk about what you would like to do after GCSEs and beyond:

En el futuro — In the future
Algún día — One day
Cuando sea mayor — When I am older
Después de los exámenes — After the exams
Si tuviera la oportunidad — If I had the opportunity (higher-level)

Key Fact

The phrase si tuviera la oportunidad, me gustaría… (if I had the opportunity, I would like…) uses the imperfect subjunctive with the conditional. This is a higher-level structure that impresses examiners. Even memorising one or two set phrases using this pattern can boost your marks significantly.

En el futuro, me gustaría casarme y tener dos hijos. Creo que el matrimonio es importante porque demuestra tu compromiso con tu pareja. Mi boda ideal sería en la playa con toda mi familia. Sin embargo, entiendo que hoy en día muchas parejas prefieren no casarse y eso también está bien. Si tuviera la oportunidad, viviría en España con mi familia porque me encanta la cultura española.

Translation: In the future, I would like to get married and have two children. I think marriage is important because it shows your commitment to your partner. My ideal wedding would be on the beach with all my family. However, I understand that nowadays many couples prefer not to get married and that is also fine. If I had the opportunity, I would live in Spain with my family because I love Spanish culture.

Notice how this model paragraph uses the conditional tense (me gustaría, sería, viviría), a si clause (si tuviera la oportunidad), opinion phrases (creo que, sin embargo, entiendo que), and future time expressions (en el futuro, hoy en día). Using multiple tenses in one response is exactly what examiners are looking for.

Eating Out in Spanish

The topic of eating out and juegos de rol (role-plays) in restaurants is tested directly in the AQA GCSE Spanish speaking exam. You need to be able to order food and drink, ask questions, deal with problems, and use polite language. This lesson covers the essential vocabulary and practises the kind of transactional language that appears in the Foundation and Higher role-play tasks.

Restaurant scenarios also appear in listening and reading papers, where you might need to understand a menu, follow a conversation between a waiter and customer, or read a restaurant review.

Restaurant Vocabulary

Starters and mains: la sopa (soup), la ensalada (salad), el pollo (chicken), el pescado (fish), la carne (meat), las patatas fritas (chips), el arroz (rice), la paella (paella), las gambas (prawns), la tortilla española (Spanish omelette), el jamón serrano (cured ham), las tapas (small dishes).

Desserts: el helado (ice cream), el flan (crème caramel), la tarta (cake), la fruta (fruit), los churros con chocolate (churros with chocolate).

Drinks: el agua (water), el zumo de naranja (orange juice), la limonada (lemonade), el café (coffee), el té (tea), un refresco (a soft drink).

Key Fact

To order in a restaurant, use: “Para mí…” (For me…), “Quisiera…” (I would like…), or “Me gustaría…” (I would like…). These are polite forms that the examiner expects you to use in a role-play. Avoid the informal “quiero” (I want) on its own — it can sound rude.

Key Phrases for the Restaurant

Learn these expresiones útiles (useful expressions) for restaurant conversations:

  • ¿Tiene una mesa para dos? — Do you have a table for two?
  • Quisiera reservar una mesa — I would like to book a table
  • ¿Qué recomienda? — What do you recommend?
  • ¿Cuál es el plato del día? — What is the dish of the day?
  • La cuenta, por favor — The bill, please
  • ¿Está incluido el servicio? — Is service included?

Dealing with Problems

In the Higher tier role-play, you may need to deal with an unexpected situation. Common problems in a restaurant include:

Hay un problema (There is a problem). El plato está frío (The dish is cold). Esto no es lo que pedí (This is not what I ordered). Falta un tenedor (A fork is missing). ¿Puede traer otro, por favor? (Can you bring another one, please?). Soy alérgico/a a… (I am allergic to…). Soy vegetariano/a (I am vegetarian). ¿Contiene frutos secos? (Does it contain nuts?).

Key Fact

The usted form is essential in restaurant role-plays. When speaking to a waiter, use the usted (formal you) form: “¿Puede traer…?” (Can you bring…?), “¿Tiene…?” (Do you have…?). This shows cultural awareness and earns marks for register.

Role-Play Practice

In the speaking exam, you receive a card with five bullet points. One will be a surprise element marked with “!”. Here is a typical restaurant role-play scenario:

Scenario: You are in a restaurant in Spain. The teacher plays the waiter.

1. Book a table for four people → “Quisiera reservar una mesa para cuatro personas, por favor.”

2. Order a starter and a main course → “De primero, quisiera la sopa. De segundo, el pollo con arroz.”

3. Ask what drinks they have → “¿Qué bebidas tienen?”

4. Say what you ate last time you visited → “La última vez comí paella y estaba muy rica.”

5. ! (Unexpected) There is a problem with your order → “Perdone, pero el plato está frío. ¿Puede cambiarlo, por favor?”

Technology in Daily Life

Technology and social media are key topics in AQA GCSE Spanish Theme 3. You need to describe how you use technology, discuss its advantages and disadvantages, and give opinions about screen time. This topic appears frequently in the writing and speaking exams.

Key Fact

the specification expects you to discuss technology across multiple tenses: what you do now (present), what you did yesterday (preterite), what you used to do (imperfect), and what you will do in the future (future tense). Using all four shows excellent range.

Key Vocabulary — Technology

el móvil — the mobile phone. un ordenador — a computer. un portátil — a laptop. la pantalla — the screen. el teclado — the keyboard. un ratón — a mouse. los videojuegos — video games. una contraseña — a password. la señal — the signal. las redes sociales — social media. un correo electrónico — an email. un mensaje — a message. la red — the internet / the web. una aplicación / una app — an app.

Saying What You Use Technology For

Use the verb usar (to use) with technology vocabulary. From the source material, key phrases include:

Uso mi móvil para comunicar con otras personas — I use my phone to communicate with other people. Mando mensajes a mi mejor amigo — I send messages to my best friend. Envío correos electrónicos — I send emails. Busco información en la red — I search for information online. Bajo mi canción favorita — I download my favourite song. Guardo mis contraseñas en secreto — I keep my passwords secret.

cada día — every day. a veces — sometimes. a menudo — often. siempre — always. normalmente — normally. una vez a la semana — once a week. por la tarde — in the afternoon/evening. antes de dormir — before sleeping.

Advantages and Disadvantages of Technology

Being able to discuss ventajas (advantages) and desventajas (disadvantages) of technology is essential for the exam:

Ventajas: Puedes mantenerte en contacto con amigos en el extranjero — You can keep in touch with friends abroad. Puedes buscar información rápidamente — You can search for information quickly. Puede ser rápida — It can be fast.

Desventajas: No es gratis — It’s not free. Puede ser lenta — It can be slow. Hay riesgos — There are risks. Hay sitios peligrosos — There are dangerous sites. A veces la señal puede ser débil — Sometimes the signal can be weak. Puede ser cara — It can be expensive.

Key Fact

Use por un lado… por otro lado… (on one hand… on the other hand…) to structure a balanced argument about technology. This connective phrase impresses examiners in both writing and speaking.

Technology in Different Tenses

The source material shows how to shift between tenses when discussing technology:

Present: Uso mi móvil cada día — I use my phone every day. Preterite: Ayer mandé mensajes a mis amigos — Yesterday I sent messages to my friends. Imperfect: Antes no tenía móvil — Before I didn’t have a phone. Future: En el futuro usaré la tecnología para trabajar — In the future I will use technology to work.

The perfect tense (haber + past participle) is useful for saying what you have done recently: He comprado — I have bought. Hemos enviado — We have sent. Ha recibido — He/she has received. Past participles: -ar verbs → -ado (comprar → comprado), -er/-ir verbs → -ido (comer → comido, vivir → vivido). Irregular: roto (broken), visto (seen).

Screen Time and Social Media

To discuss screen time and its effects: Paso demasiado tiempo en mi móvil — I spend too much time on my phone. Debería usar menos las redes sociales — I should use social media less. Es importante apagar el móvil antes de dormir — It’s important to turn off your phone before sleeping.

Key Fact

The source material provides this model: “Siempre apago mi móvil antes de dormir.” (I always turn off my phone before sleeping.) Use apagar (to turn off) and encender (to turn on) — these are common listening exam words.

Weather Vocabulary

Being able to describe the weather is essential for the AQA GCSE Spanish exam. Weather links naturally to holidays, outdoor activities, and daily life. You need to recognise weather phrases in listening and reading, and use them in speaking and writing tasks.

Hace sol — It’s sunny. Hace calor — It’s hot. Hace frío — It’s cold. Hace buen tiempo — The weather is good. Hace mal tiempo — The weather is bad. Hace viento — It’s windy. Llueve — It’s raining. Nieva — It’s snowing. Hay niebla — It’s foggy. Hay tormenta — There’s a storm. Está nublado — It’s cloudy.

Key Fact

Spanish uses different verbs for weather: hace (from hacer) for most expressions, llueve/nieva as standalone verbs, hay for fog and storms, and está for cloudy. Don’t mix these up in the exam.

Weather in Different Tenses

To talk about past weather, change hace to hacía (imperfect) or hizo (preterite): Hacía sol — It was sunny. Hizo buen tiempo — The weather was good. For future weather: Hará calor — It will be hot. Va a llover — It’s going to rain.

Holiday Activities

The specification requires you to describe activities you do on holiday. Here are essential phrases from the teacher resources:

tomar el sol — to sunbathe. nadar en el mar — to swim in the sea. montar en bici — to ride a bike. hacer deporte — to do sport. hacer turismo — to do sightseeing. ir de compras — to go shopping. comprar recuerdos — to buy souvenirs. salir a cenar — to go out for dinner. bailar en la discoteca — to dance in the nightclub. hacer camping — to go camping. descansar — to rest. visitar un museo — to visit a museum. tomar fotos — to take photos. montar a caballo — to go horse riding. comer comida deliciosa — to eat delicious food.

Describing What You Did on Holiday — Past Tenses

Use the preterite for completed actions: Nadé en el mar. Compré recuerdos. Fui de compras. Use the imperfect for descriptions and ongoing actions: Hacía sol. El mar era muy bonito.

Key Fact

A model past holiday paragraph: “El verano pasado fui de vacaciones a la playa. Hacía sol y el agua estaba clara. Cada mañana nadábamos en el mar y por la tarde tomábamos el sol.” Notice how the preterite (fui) and imperfect (hacía, nadábamos) are combined.

The Past Continuous

The past continuous describes what was happening at a specific moment. It is formed with estar in the imperfect + the gerund (-ando for -ar verbs, -iendo for -er/-ir verbs).

Examples: Estaba nadando — I was swimming. Estábamos comiendo — We were eating. Estaban bailando — They were dancing. Estaba descansando cuando empezó a llover — I was resting when it started to rain.

yo estaba + gerund. tú estabas + gerund. él/ella estaba + gerund. nosotros estábamos + gerund. vosotros estabais + gerund. ellos/ellas estaban + gerund. For -ar verbs: add -ando (nadar → nadando). For -er/-ir verbs: add -iendo (comer → comiendo, vivir → viviendo).

Key Fact

The past continuous is very useful for scene-setting in writing: “Estaba tomando el sol en la playa cuando empezó a llover.” (I was sunbathing on the beach when it started to rain.) This combination of past continuous + preterite impresses examiners.

Talking About Free Time

One of the most common topics in the AQA GCSE Spanish exam is el tiempo libre. You need to be able to describe what you do in your free time, give opinions about activities, and use a range of tenses. This lesson focuses on the present tense — what you do regularly — and builds the core vocabulary you will need throughout Theme 2.

In the exam, you might be asked to write about your hobbies in a letter, describe a photo showing leisure activities, or translate sentences about free-time routines. Being confident with this vocabulary is essential for both the writing and speaking papers.

Key Fact

In Spanish, to say what you like doing, use me gusta + infinitive: “Me gusta jugar al fútbol” (I like playing football). To say what you love doing, use me encanta + infinitive: “Me encanta leer” (I love reading).

Key Vocabulary: Hobbies and Activities

Sports: jugar al fútbol (play football), jugar al baloncesto (play basketball), nadar (swim), correr (run), montar en bicicleta (ride a bike), hacer atletismo (do athletics), jugar al tenis (play tennis), hacer gimnasia (do gymnastics).

Indoor activities: leer (read), ver la televisión (watch TV), escuchar música (listen to music), jugar con videojuegos (play video games), cocinar (cook), dibujar (draw), tocar la guitarra (play the guitar).

Going out: salir con amigos (go out with friends), ir al cine (go to the cinema), ir de compras (go shopping), pasear (go for a walk), ir a la bolera (go bowling).

The Present Tense: Regular Verbs

To describe what you do regularly, you need the presente (present tense). Spanish has three verb groups: -ar, -er, and -ir verbs. Each group has its own set of endings.

-AR verbs (e.g. jugar — to play): yo juego, tú juegas, él/ella juega, nosotros jugamos, vosotros jugáis, ellos juegan.

-ER verbs (e.g. comer — to eat): yo como, tú comes, él/ella come, nosotros comemos, vosotros coméis, ellos comen.

-IR verbs (e.g. vivir — to live): yo vivo, tú vives, él/ella vive, nosotros vivimos, vosotros vivís, ellos viven.

Giving Opinions About Hobbies

The exam rewards students who give and justify opinions. Here are key frases de opinión (opinion phrases) you should memorise:

  • Me gusta (I like) / No me gusta (I don’t like)
  • Me encanta (I love) / Me aburre (It bores me)
  • Prefiero (I prefer) + infinitive
  • Me interesa (It interests me) / Me molesta (It annoys me)

Always follow an opinion with porque (because) and a reason: “Me gusta nadar porque es relajante” (I like swimming because it is relaxing).

Key Fact

To impress the examiner, vary your opinion phrases. Instead of always writing “me gusta,” use alternatives like “lo que más me gusta es” (what I like most is), “lo paso bomba cuando” (I have a great time when), or “me resulta divertido” (I find it fun).

Frequency Words

Using adverbios de frecuencia (frequency adverbs) adds detail to your answers and shows the examiner you can vary your language:

  • Siempre (always), a menudo (often), normalmente (normally), a veces (sometimes), de vez en cuando (from time to time), raramente (rarely), nunca (never).

Example: “Normalmente juego al fútbol los sábados, pero a veces voy al cine con mis amigos.” (Normally I play football on Saturdays, but sometimes I go to the cinema with my friends.)

En mi tiempo libre, me encanta jugar al fútbol con mis amigos. Normalmente jugamos los sábados por la mañana en el parque. También me gusta escuchar música porque es relajante. A veces veo películas en casa, pero no me gusta mucho jugar con videojuegos porque me resulta aburrido. Los domingos suelo salir con mi familia — vamos de paseo o vamos de compras al centro.

Translation: In my free time, I love playing football with my friends. We normally play on Saturday mornings in the park. I also like listening to music because it is relaxing. Sometimes I watch films at home, but I don’t really like playing video games because I find it boring. On Sundays I usually go out with my family — we go for a walk or go shopping in town.

Sport and Exercise in Spanish

Sport and exercise is a topic that overlaps with both Theme 2 (Popular Culture) and Theme 4 (Health) in the AQA GCSE Spanish specification. You need to be able to name sports, describe exercise routines, and explain why physical activity is important. This lesson builds the vocabulario (vocabulary) you need and practises using key verb structures.

The exam might ask you to describe a photo of people playing sport, write about your exercise habits, or translate sentences about keeping fit. Strong vocabulary and accurate verb use are essential for scoring well.

Key Sport Vocabulary

Team sports: el fútbol (football), el baloncesto (basketball), el voleibol (volleyball), el rugby (rugby), el hockey (hockey), el cricket (cricket).

Individual sports: la natación (swimming), el atletismo (athletics), el ciclismo (cycling), la gimnasia (gymnastics), el boxeo (boxing), las artes marciales (martial arts), el esquí (skiing).

Exercise activities: correr (to run), caminar (to walk), hacer ejercicio (to exercise), ir al gimnasio (to go to the gym), hacer yoga (to do yoga), montar en bicicleta (to ride a bike), patinar (to skate).

Key Fact

In Spanish, you use jugar a for ball/team sports (“juego al fútbol”) but hacer for individual activities (“hago natación”). Getting the right verb + preposition combination is important for accuracy marks in the exam.

Key Verbs: Jugar, Hacer, Practicar

Three verbs are central to talking about sport. Jugar (a) means to play (a sport). Hacer means to do or make. Practicar means to practise or do (a sport). Notice that jugar is a stem-changing verb — the “u” changes to “ue” in most present tense forms:

  • yo juego, tú juegas, él/ella juega, nosotros jugamos, ellos juegan

Hacer is also irregular in the first person: yo hago (I do). The other forms are regular: haces, hace, hacemos, hacen.

Describing How Often You Exercise

Combining sport vocabulary with time expressions makes your writing more detailed. Use phrases like:

  • Todos los días (every day), dos veces a la semana (twice a week), los fines de semana (at weekends), después del instituto (after school), por la mañana temprano (early in the morning).

Why Exercise Is Important

In the exam, you may need to explain why sport matters. Key reasons in Spanish include:

Es bueno para la salud (It’s good for your health). Me mantiene en forma (It keeps me fit). Reduce el estrés (It reduces stress). Es una buena manera de relajarse (It’s a good way to relax). Me da energía (It gives me energy). Es divertido y social (It’s fun and social). Mejora la concentración (It improves concentration).

Key Fact

To reach higher mark bands, use connectives and complex structures: “Hago deporte no solo porque es divertido, sino también porque me mantiene en forma y reduce el estrés.” (I do sport not only because it’s fun, but also because it keeps me fit and reduces stress.) The structure no solo… sino también impresses examiners.

Using Multiple Tenses

To access the top marks in writing and speaking, you must use at least three tiempos verbales (tenses). Here is how to talk about sport in different tenses:

Present: “Juego al fútbol dos veces a la semana.” (I play football twice a week.)

Preterite (past): “Ayer jugué al tenis con mi hermano.” (Yesterday I played tennis with my brother.)

Future: “El año que viene voy a hacer más ejercicio.” (Next year I am going to do more exercise.) You can also use the simple future: “Haré más deporte.” (I will do more sport.)

Unhealthy Habits — Las Malas Costumbres

The AQA GCSE Spanish specification requires you to discuss unhealthy lifestyle habits including smoking, alcohol, drugs and vaping. This topic appears in reading, listening and writing tasks. You need to understand opinions about these habits and be able to give advice using structures like se debe and hay que.

Key Fact

Se debe + infinitive means “one must” or “you should”. No se debe + infinitive means “one must not”. For example: No se debe fumar (One must not smoke). Se debe evitar las drogas (One should avoid drugs).

fumar — to smoke | vapear — to vape | beber alcohol — to drink alcohol | drogarse — to take drugs | el tabaco / el cigarrillo — tobacco / cigarette | la droga — drug | el alcohol — alcohol | emborracharse — to get drunk | el/la drogadicto/a — drug addict | la drogadicción — drug addiction | las drogas blandas — soft drugs | las drogas duras — hard drugs | peligroso/a — dangerous | el riesgo — risk | la salud — health | malo/a para la salud — bad for health | dejar de fumar — to quit smoking | un veneno — a poison

Opinions on Smoking — El Tabaco

Smoking is one of the most common topics in AQA reading and listening texts about health. You need to recognise both reasons people give for smoking and reasons against it.

Reasons people smoke: Te hace sentir más adulto (It makes you feel more grown-up). Me relaja (It relaxes me). Me da confianza (It gives me confidence). Todos en mi clase fuman (Everyone in my class smokes). Se burlan de mí si no fumo (They make fun of me if I don’t smoke).

Reasons not to smoke: Es un veneno (It is a poison). Hay riesgo de cáncer (There is a risk of cancer). Es malo para la salud (It is bad for health). Te da mal aliento (It gives you bad breath). Los dientes y las uñas se hacen amarillos (Your teeth and nails turn yellow). Es un malgasto / cuesta mucho (It is a waste of money / it costs a lot).

Key Fact

The health effects of smoking in Spanish include: cáncer de pulmón (lung cancer), cáncer de garganta (throat cancer), dolor en el pecho (chest pain), tos del fumador (smoker’s cough), and mala circulación (poor circulation). These terms appear frequently in AQA reading comprehension texts.

Alcohol and Drugs — El Alcohol y Las Drogas

The specification also covers alcohol consumption and drug use. You may encounter reading texts where young people discuss their views on these issues.

Key phrases about alcohol: El alcohol afecta a las emociones (Alcohol affects emotions). Produce mala pronunciación al hablar (It causes slurred speech). Afecta a la memoria (It affects memory). Puede causar cáncer del estómago (It can cause stomach cancer). El abuso de alcohol (Alcohol abuse).

Opinions on drugs: Es peligroso (It’s dangerous). Es tonto (It’s stupid). Puedes morir (You can die). Nadie sabe los efectos (Nobody knows the effects). Es un problema enorme (It’s a huge problem).

“A mi modo de ver, fumar cigarrillos es inofensivo. Fumo con mis amigos porque te hace sentir más adulto. Creo que se puede dejar fácilmente.” — Felipe

“Por un lado pienso que hay muchos riesgos si fumas. Mi abuelo sufrió del cáncer de los pulmones, porque fumaba cuando era joven. Por otro lado, todos en mi clase fuman.” — Maripi

Felipe thinks smoking is harmless and smokes with friends to feel more adult. Maripi recognises the risks — her grandfather suffered from lung cancer — but acknowledges peer pressure. These contrasting views are typical of AQA reading texts.

Giving Advice — Se Debe, Hay Que, Es Importante

A key grammar skill for this topic is giving impersonal advice. These structures allow you to make general recommendations without specifying a person.

Se debe + infinitive — One must / You should: Se debe evitar las drogas (You should avoid drugs). | No se debe + infinitive — One must not: No se debe fumar (You must not smoke). | Hay que + infinitive — It is necessary to: Hay que decir ‘no’ (You have to say ‘no’). | Es importante + infinitive — It is important to: Es importante cuidar la salud (It is important to look after your health). | Es necesario + infinitive — It is necessary to. | Es aconsejable + infinitive — It is advisable to. | Es imprescindible + infinitive — It is essential to.

Using these structures in your writing shows the examiner that you can handle impersonal constructions, which is a higher-level grammar skill. Try to include at least one in any writing task about health.

Key Fact

The text “Fumar sigue siendo un problema grave entre los jóvenes” (Smoking continues to be a serious problem among young people) is a strong opening for a writing task on this topic. Using phrases like sigue siendo (continues to be) and entre los jóvenes (among young people) will impress examiners.

Vaping — Vapear

Vaping is a modern topic that appears increasingly in AQA exam materials. Key vocabulary includes: vapear (to vape), el cigarrillo electrónico (e-cigarette), animar a los jóvenes a fumar (encourage young people to smoke). A typical exam text might say: “Vapear es muy malo para la salud” (Vaping is very bad for your health).

You should also know: No vapeo (I don’t vape), Dejé de vapear (I stopped vaping), and El vapeo puede causar problemas respiratorios (Vaping can cause breathing problems).

School Rules — Las Reglas del Instituto

The AQA GCSE Spanish specification requires you to discuss school rules. You need to understand and produce sentences about what is and isn’t allowed at school, using structures like se debe, no se debe, se puede, and tengo que.

no se debe comer chicle — you must not chew gum | no se debe comer en clase — you must not eat in class | no se debe fumar — you must not smoke | no se debe llevar maquillaje — you must not wear make-up | no se puede ir al baño durante las clases — you cannot go to the toilet during lessons | no se puede utilizar el móvil — you cannot use your mobile phone | se debe llevar el uniforme correcto — you must wear the correct uniform | se debe tratar a los alumnos y profesores con respeto — you must treat students and teachers with respect | no se debe hablar cuando habla el profesor — you must not talk when the teacher is talking | se debe levantar la mano — you must raise your hand

Key Fact

There are several structures for expressing obligation and prohibition in Spanish: Se debe + infinitive (one must), No se debe + infinitive (one must not), Se puede (one can), No se puede (one cannot), Tengo que + infinitive (I have to), Debo + infinitive (I must). Using a mix of these in your writing shows grammatical range.

A typical dictation or reading task about school rules: “En mi insti, hay muchas reglas. No se debe comer en clase, llevar maquillaje y se debe tratar a todos los alumnos y profesores con respeto. Mis profesores son muy estrictos.”

Homework — Los Deberes

Homework is a common topic in AQA listening and reading texts. You need to understand opinions about homework and be able to discuss it in writing.

Key phrases about homework: Tenemos muchos deberes (We have a lot of homework). Tengo demasiados deberes (I have too much homework). Hago los deberes todas las tardes (I do homework every evening). Los deberes son aburridos pero necesarios (Homework is boring but necessary). No me gusta hacer deberes (I don’t like doing homework). Paso dos horas haciendo deberes (I spend two hours doing homework).

Key Fact

Los deberes is always plural in Spanish, even though we say “homework” (singular) in English. So you say Los deberes son difíciles (Homework is difficult), not *El deber es difícil.

The Future Tense — El Futuro

To discuss plans after school, you need the future tense. There are two main ways to express future plans in Spanish.

1. Near Future — Ir a + Infinitive

The near future is the simplest way to talk about plans. It uses ir (to go) + a + infinitive: Voy a estudiar (I am going to study). Voy a ir a la universidad (I am going to go to university).

voy a (I am going to) | vas a (you are going to) | va a (he/she is going to) | vamos a (we are going to) | vais a (you all are going to) | van a (they are going to)

Examples: Voy a hacer el bachillerato (I am going to do A-levels). Mi amigo va a trabajar (My friend is going to work). Vamos a continuar con nuestra educación (We are going to continue with our education).

2. Simple Future Tense

The simple future tense is formed by adding endings to the infinitive. This is a higher-level structure that impresses examiners:

Endings: -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án. Example with estudiar: estudiaré (I will study), estudiarás (you will study), estudiará (he/she will study), estudiaremos (we will study), estudiaréis (you all will study), estudiarán (they will study).

Key Fact

The simple future tense uses the WHOLE infinitive as the stem (e.g. estudiar + é = estudiaré). This works for all regular -ar, -er, and -ir verbs. Some common irregular stems: tener → tendr-, hacer → har-, ir → ir-, poder → podr-, querer → querr-.

Future Plans — Planes para el Futuro

The specification requires you to discuss what you will do after school. Here are the key future plan phrases:

En el futuro me gustaría... — In the future I would like... | Después del instituto voy a... — After secondary school I am going to... | Cuando termine el insti quiero... — When I finish school, I want to... | ir a la universidad — to go to university | hacer el bachillerato — to do A-levels (baccalaureate) | hacer un curso de formación profesional — to do an apprenticeship | continuar con mi educación — to continue with my education | trabajar — to work | ganar experiencia laboral — to gain work experience | ganar dinero — to earn money

Reasons for choices: porque quiero aprender una profesión útil (because I want to learn a useful trade) | porque quiero ganar dinero (because I want to earn money) | porque me gusta estudiar (because I like studying) | porque quiero un horario flexible (because I want a flexible schedule) | porque quiero un buen trabajo (because I want a good job).

English to Spanish:

In the future, I would like to work because I want a flexible schedule. → En el futuro me gustaría trabajar porque quiero un horario flexible.

When I finish school, I want to do an apprenticeship because I want to earn money. → Cuando termine el insti, quiero hacer un curso de formación profesional porque quiero ganar dinero.

After secondary school, I am going to continue with my education. → Después del instituto voy a continuar con mi educación.

Key Fact

In writing tasks, using both the near future (voy a + infinitive) AND the simple future tense (estudiaré) shows the examiner you can handle multiple tenses. Also include the conditional (me gustaría — I would like) for extra credit. Mixing tenses is one of the best ways to reach higher mark bands.
